questions.stem: A serious machine incident occurs, and production wants to clean the area immediately. Emergency hazards are controlled and the injured employee has been transported. What should the investigation leader do next?

Discard damaged components once photographs are taken
Interview witnesses together while they discuss and harmonize their recollections
Return the equipment to service before documenting it so investigators can observe normal production

The option 'Interview witnesses together while they discuss and harmonize their recollections' does not apply the controlling principle for scene control and evidence preservation to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Return the equipment to service before documenting it so investigators can observe normal production' does not apply the controlling principle for scene control and evidence preservation to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: Three witnesses saw different portions of an incident. Which interview method is most likely to produce reliable information?

Interview them separately as soon as practical using open questions, then clarify sequence, observations, and uncertainty without leading
Interview them as a group so they can agree on one account
Ask only yes-or-no questions and stop once the first consistent answer is obtained
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Separate, timely, nonleading interviews reduce memory contamination and allow investigators to distinguish observation, inference, and uncertainty.

The option 'Interview them as a group so they can agree on one account' does not apply the controlling principle for witness interviewing to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Ask only yes-or-no questions and stop once the first consistent answer is obtained' does not apply the controlling principle for witness interviewing to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: An employee bypassed a guard before an injury. The investigation stops at “employee failed to follow procedure.” What is the strongest critique?
options: Exclude human actions from causal analysis and focus the investigation only on physical equipment conditions
Close the investigation once the rule violation is documented and assign retraining as the corrective action
The conclusion identifies an act but does not examine why bypass was possible or attractive, including design, production pressure, supervision, and procedure quality
Treat the guard bypass as proof that equipment design and production conditions did not contribute
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: A useful causal analysis examines system conditions that shape behavior and barrier failure rather than treating the last unsafe act as the full explanation.
incorrectOptionExplanations: The option 'Exclude human actions from causal analysis and focus the investigation only on physical equipment conditions' does not apply the controlling principle for root cause versus immediate cause to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Close the investigation once the rule violation is documented and assign retraining as the corrective action' does not apply the controlling principle for root cause versus immediate cause to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

The option 'Treat the guard bypass as proof that equipment design and production conditions did not contribute' does not apply the controlling principle for root cause versus immediate cause to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.

questions.stem: A chemical transfer relied on a level alarm, operator response, and an overflow line. All three failed during a release. Which analysis best supports prevention?
options: Replace only the operator because human error is the sole barrier type
Add another alarm on the same failed power supply without reviewing independence
Calculate injury rates and omit the physical safeguards from the investigation
Examine each barrier’s intended function, independence, condition, failure mode, and management controls, including common-cause weaknesses

The option 'Calculate injury rates and omit the physical safeguards from the investigation' does not apply the controlling principle for barrier analysis to the facts given, so it is not the best answer.
